cis_text.title: Train Workforce on Data Handling Best Practices

ai_guidance.llm: Train users not to enter sensitive, regulated, or proprietary data into unapproved AI systems or public AI chat interfaces. Users must understand the differences between enterprise-approved models and consumer-facing tools, and how data retention or reuse in those systems may violate policy.
ai_guidance.agent: Reinforce safe interaction patterns for end-users. Train business users on safe ways to interact with agents, including verifying outputs, avoiding over-reliance, understanding limitations, and recognizing when agent recommendations may be unsafe or out of scope.
ai_guidance.mcp: Train staff on data handling rules for prompts and outputs including classification tags, redaction requirements, and clear guidance against pasting secrets. Include guidance on risky input types such as uploaded files, images, and embedded links that may contain embedded prompt injection or manipulation payloads. Ensure staff understand why environment separation matters, using staging for evaluation and keeping production data strictly within defined boundaries.

limits: A claim shows that a control can mitigate a technique. It does not show that an implementation is effective.
'none' or 'no_row' means the mapping has no mitigating control. It does not mean that no defence exists.
Claims use ATT&CK Enterprise 16.1, the version that the source mapping uses. See later_version for changes in newer versions.
CIS claims (cis_claims and cis/safeguards) use ATT&CK Enterprise 19.1, the version that the CIS mapping uses.

ATLAS results describe the ATLAS release in versions.atlas, pinned by commit and digest. ATLAS changes often: a later release can add techniques and mitigations. An empty mitigation list means that this release links no mitigation, not that no mitigation exists. agent_related is derived by this project from names.
